title: Maya's AML quant & eval scratchpad — daily runnotes
content:
Quick log (fast, messy) — working through a few micro-experiments for 4-bit/8-bit quantized variants and prompt sensitivity. Goal: identify regressions that matter for customer-facing chat and reranker workloads; figure out a minimal canary eval suite that catches quality regressions after quant + kernel changes.

2026-03-12 — morning
- Ran baseline evals on redwood-13b-vanilla (fp16) to re-establish numbers after infra tweak (cuda driver update).
  * dataset: small_chat_eval_v3 (200 examples, mixed instruction/chat style)
  * metric: ROUGE-L / BLEU not great for chat — using response rank and 3-judge sign-off subset; also perplexity on held-out.
  * baseline fp16: avg_response_rank=0.82, mean_perplexity=12.4

- Quick 4-bit qint8-like run using q4_k_m (hf fork):
  $ python run_eval.py --model redwood-13b-q4 --quant q4_k_m --batch 8 --seq 1024 --eval-set small_chat_eval_v3 --out results/q4-m-20260312.json
  * observed: avg_response_rank=0.79 (delta -0.03), mean_perplexity=13.1 (small increase)
  * subjective: answers slightly shorter, occasionally omits clarifying question.
  * runtime: ~0.95x baseline per-token latency (good), GPU memory ~22GB (fits in 24GB node)

Notes: the drop seems concentrated on multi-turn clarification cases. Hypothesis: quantized attention weights reduce softmax sharpness -> more likely to choose safe/short reply. Need to compare logits distribution.

2026-03-12 — midday experiment (prompt-level ablation)
- Prompts: tested two variants to encourage elaboration:
  A) "Please explain steps and ask at least one follow-up question."
  B) "Give a short answer."
- q4 model responded to A with more compliant behavior after adding a short chain-of-thought hint ("first list steps, then ask a question"). Suggests prompts can ameliorate quality loss for certain use-cases.

Commands used (notes):
- export CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0
- python -m venv .venv_eval && source .venv_eval/bin/activate
- pip install -r requirements-eval.txt (hf-transformers-lock, safetensors, triton@local)

2026-03-12 — late afternoon, 8-bit dynamic (fake 8-bit emulation)
- q8_dynamic run: avg_response_rank=0.81, perplexity=12.7.
- memory: ~27GB (just over 24GB) -> needs 32GB nodes for stable throughput.
- latency: 1.07x baseline.

Observations so far:
- q4_k_m gives best memory savings and keeps latency low, but has small, non-trivial quality drop on clarifying/multi-turn items.
- q8 dynamic is safer quality-wise but requires bigger nodes (cost tradeoff).
- Prompt engineering helps; consider shipping a small prompting shim for sensitive endpoints (can we do this without breaking API semantics?)

To-do (short-term):
- [ ] Dump logits for 50 multi-turn cases for fp16 vs q4_k_m to inspect distribution + top-k entropy. (ticket: JIRA-AML-674)
- [ ] Add 2-shot examples in canary eval to measure few-shot robustness (create small_fewshot_eval_50).
- [ ] Re-run q4 with different kernel (q4_0 vs q4_k_m) — compare.
- [ ] Try per-layer mixed precision: keep first 2 layers fp16, rest q4; test memory and quality.
- [ ] Add smoke test for 'asks follow-up' metric to automated canary (binary: did model ask a question within first 3 sentences).

Open questions / weirdness:
- Why do some runs show lower perplexity but worse human-rated response_rank? Perplexity doesn't capture pragmatic fallbacks. Need human or proxy metric tuned to helpfulness.
- Is there any interaction with KV cache warm-up across batches? Saw occasional cold-start flakiness where first response is extremely short; might be batching or stale cache reuse.

Experiment artifacts locations:
- results/ (local) -> q4-m-20260312.json, q8-dyn-20260312.json
- logs/ -> eval-run-20260312.log (grep "ERROR: kv_cache")
- temp/ -> small_chat_eval_v3_subset.csv (manual selection)

Quick checklist for next pairing session with Noah:
- Walk through logits dump script: scripts/logit_diff.py (explain columns and expected range)
- Set up a small live demo where we can toggle quantization and compare responses in browser (fast client proxy).
- Decide on cost threshold for shipping q8 vs q4 for Dedicated customers.

Notes to self (random):
- If using q4_k_m, try increasing sampling temp from 0.7 -> 0.85 for clarifying prompts; might reduce short replies.
- Remember: don't conflate slight perplexity increase with catastrophic failure — user-facing threshold is task-dependent.

Minor housekeeping:
- push results/ to the experiment bucket and tag with "quant-q4-20260312"
- make a small README in results/ describing eval set and metric definitions (rank, mrr, perplexity)

End-of-day quick reflections:
- I think we can safely pursue q4 for non-sensitive batch tasks (embeddings/rerank precompute) and keep q8 for chat endpoints where latency/cost allows. Next week focus: formalize canary with 200 multi-turn examples and an automated slack alert when response_rank drops > 0.02 vs baseline.

-- maya

(ps: this is messy on purpose — use as running log for experiments. If it stabilizes into a proper doc I'll move to shared_drives/engineering/applied-ml.)
